In this episode of Outside Inside Outside Racing, Ian cut the side vent section out of Sr. Dos to save the Goblin and to start preparing Sr. Dos for its next life as a development mule for AW11 MR2 2AR engine swaps.

Before it heads off we tackle:

Then we check in on the Goblin… which hasn’t run in months.

Spoiler: Good old 4AGE.

After that, it’s time to look at the 2026 RallyCross prep list:
 • Thermostat install
 • Full coolant baseline (yes… bleeding an MR2 again 😐)
 • Pre-season nut and bolt check
 • Steering rack swap
 • Quality of life upgrades

This is the transition moment. Sr. Dos becomes a sacrifice for the future. The Goblin gets closer to 2026 RallyCross duty. And the 2AR swap dream moves forward.

title: Will This 80s Icon Run Again? - AW11 MR2 Rallycross Rescue
description:
Ian's 1985 AW11 MR2 we call THE GOBLIN gave everything it had in 20 runs at the last Kansas City SCCA rallycross event… right up until the moment it didn’t. After a full day of ripping through the dirt, it refused to fire back up. Since then it’s been sitting with Marvel Mystery Oil soaking in the cylinders, but the big question remains: will it ever run again?

In this episode, we dig into the little mid-engine Toyota to see what actually went wrong. Bad spark plugs were discovered, the ignition system gets a closer look, and we walk through the first real attempt to revive the car after its dramatic shutdown.

If it comes back to life, the next challenge is getting it ready for winter including draining the straight water that’s in the system and replacing it with a proper 50/50 coolant mix before the freeze hits. #winteriscoming

Only old cars are allowed, all pre-1968, and the pits are filled with the kind of machines that built drag racing history.

Every detail is designed to capture the spirit of the era. Drivers suit up in period-style gear, the cars wear vintage paint and lettering, and the atmosphere is pure old school. The Rumble is more than a car show, it is a living museum that blasts past at over 100 mph, and if you are anywhere near northern Missouri, it is an event you do not want to miss.

Cheap DIY Mod That Could Save Your Motor | 1972 Toyota Celica
description:
After losing rod bearings in his 1972 Toyota Celica at an autocross, Ian realized something important: the stock oil pressure gauge is too slow to save an engine. That’s why in this video, he installs a low oil pressure switch, warning light, and buzzer. A setup we now call... the Danger Buzzer.

This simple combo activates the moment oil pressure drops below 5 psi, giving you an unmistakable, instant warning. Whether you’re tracking your vintage ride or just want peace of mind on the street, this is a cheap upgrade that could save your engine.

⸻

Parts Used in This Video:

Brass Tee Fitting Adapter (BPT to NPT)
Amazon: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0DKFG6BJN
Allows you to install both the factory sender and the new switch without deleting anything.

Beck/Arnley (Standard Motor Products) Oil Pressure Switch (5 PSI, Normally Closed)
Amazon: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B000CB246A
Closes the circuit when pressure drops, triggering the warning system.

LED Buzzer Light Combo (12V, 85 dB)
Amazon: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B01CIO8E5S
Lights up red and lets out a sharp warning buzz when activated.

Permatex High Performance Thread Sealant
Amazon: https://www.amazon.com/Permatex-56521-Performance-Thread-Sealant/dp/B000FW7VH
Seals tapered threads without interfering with electrical ground.

⸻

 You’ll Also Need:
 • Wire (preferably black/red)
 • Spade connectors or plug terminals
 • Wire strippers and crimpers
 • Wrenches to match your sender, switch, and tee
 • A bit of patience

⸻

This upgrade is especially valuable for older engines, autocross cars, or anything without a fast-reacting oil pressure warning. Don’t wait for a gauge to tell you too late. Wire in a Danger Buzzer and get ahead of the problem!

title: FWD vs RWD in a 48 Lap Endurocross Racing Showdown!
description:
Endurocross is no ordinary rallycross. With three laps per run and 16 total runs per car, it’s a brutal test of machine, driver, and patience. In this Kansas Region SCCA event at Mcain’s Off-Road Park in Carbondale KS, we put two cars on the opposite end of the RX spectrum to the test: Ian’s “Goblin” MR2 in Modified Rear-Wheel Drive, and Ryan’s daily-driven, heavily upgraded GD3 Honda Fit in Modified Front-Wheel Drive. Both cars were pushed hard all day across sticky mud, changing grip conditions, and 2 different courses.

What started as a last minute decision to run the MR2 turned into a full day of reliable performance. Meanwhile, the Fit continued to prove why it’s one of the most underrated motorsports platforms out there. With co-drivers in each car, temperamental power plants and a rerun redemption arc, this event could be the perfect showcase of grassroots motorsport durability, or a perfect guide to "how to kill your race car".

description:
AKA: What to expect when you're inspecting.
Let Ryan walk you through the new Tech Inspection process for Kansas City Region SCCA Rallycross events in 2020 and beyond. He covers car clean out, seatbelts, brakes, wheels, bearings, ball joints, battery, helmet specs and class/number display.

All of the actual safety regulations can be found in section 3.2 of the 2020 SCCA Rallycross rules here: https://www.scca.com/downloads/48333-2020-scca-rally-cross-rules/download. Next time we'll actually read them first.

UPDATE!: It was brought to our attention in the comments that duct/duck/gorilla tape is all conductive to a certain degree. Most importantly none of it is NOT conductive. Use electrical tape to cover your positive terminal if you absolutely have to, otherwise get a set of these and zip tie them on https://www.amazon.com/Fastronix-Black-Flexible-Battery-Terminal/dp/B011CO8806/ref=sr_1_3?keywords=battery+terminal+covers&qid=1582173375&sr=8-3

Check the table here if you are unsure if your helmet will work https://www.scca.com/downloads/48190-2020-solo-helmet-certification-labels-2019-11-08/download?fbclid=IwAR2XTr-tXyCG_DI7EnCVM9dZdPkxAdToP0sTlWALcOW7TxJh2l8aIGawpy0
